incident_spec.summary: Unpredictable single insert performance due to blocking and excessive indexes.
symptoms: Single record insert takes over 7 minutes.
Blocking session IDs appear in `sys.dm_exec_requests` but are not active.
incident_spec.mechanism: Blocking caused by uncommitted transactions holding locks, compounded by excessive indexes.

facts.evidence: The table is described as having 8 million rows.
The table has 34 indexes despite being an OLTP system.
Blocking sessions are reported as sleeping in `dm_exec_sessions`.

assumptions: The blocking is caused by uncommitted transactions holding locks.
Excessive indexes contribute to the poor insert performance.
unknowns: Exact schema of the table and indexes.
Specific workload patterns leading to blocking.

feasibility.rationale: The reproduction can simulate blocking and index contention, but exact schema and workload patterns are unavailable.

schema_sql: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS Communication (id INT PRIMARY KEY, comm_action NVARCHAR(255), comm_channelid INT, payload NVARCHAR(MAX))
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_comm_action ON Communication(comm_action)
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_comm_channelid ON Communication(comm_channelid)
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_payload ON Communication(payload)
generation_sql: INSERT INTO Communication (id, comm_action, comm_channelid, payload) SELECT n, CASE WHEN MOD(n, 1000)=0 THEN N'Deskwork' ELSE N'Other' END, MOD(n, 50), CONCAT(N'Payload_', n) FROM generated_numbers WHERE n <= {row_count}
